newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian banks extend gains on merger speculation.
newsitem.headline: Belgian banks extend gains on merger speculation.

text.p: Shares in the major Belgian banks extended gains on Tuesday as investors bought on rumours of a possible merger between the country's largest bank Generale Bank and rival BBL.
"People are hoping that there will be a merger, we don't have any other reason for the rise other than merger speculation," said a trader.
Dealers welcomed a possible merger saying it would strengthen the Belgian banking sector in the face of increased competition from European banks.
By 1300 GMT, Generale Bank was up 1.82 percent at 14,000 francs after earlier climbing over 3.16 percent, while BBL had gained 0.85 percent to 8,270 francs.

Generale Bank rose 4.96 percent on Monday after its controlling shareholder Societe Generale de Belgique (SGB) reiterated in an interview that it would support a merger with BBL, though it said there were no merger talks underway.
SGB was up 0.87 percent at 2,905 francs on Tuesday after slipping Monday on the merger report.
Other banks also benefited. Kredietbank gained 1.9 percent to 13,375 francs after earlier rising 2.8 percent.
Dexia CC -- which is already in a cross border alliance with Credit Local de France -- was up 2.31 percent at 4,030 francs.
Some dealers said Dexia's rise was partly due to the issue last week by Morgan Stanley of call warrants on its share and associated covering of positions.
